summary: Find hyperimmune-free paths and PA degrees, then combine two basis theorems to avoid computing any prescribed noncomputable set.
abstract: A computable binary tree can have infinite paths while having no computable path. Can one choose a path whose total numerical computations still have ordinary computable bounds? Such a path is called hyperimmune-free, and the hyperimmune-free basis theorem gives one whenever the tree has a node at every length. The key is that a program halting on every path of a fixed computable tree has a computable bound on its outputs, obtained by searching finite levels for successful computation certificates. Retaining suitable divergence restrictions then treats every oracle program while preserving a common path. Applying this to the binary diagonal-avoidance tree gives a noncomputable hyperimmune-free oracle that computes a complete consistent extension of Peano arithmetic. Such an oracle cannot be computed from the ordinary halting problem, so these choices also illustrate how computable finite searches can coexist with an uncomputable selection of an infinite path. Combining this selection with the low basis theorem also shows that every nonempty computable binary path class has a member that avoids computing any given noncomputable set.
